cards.explanation: The answer is that they do more harm than good. Paul says, “…your gatherings do more harm than good.” (1 Corinthians 11:17) He's not grumbling about a small thing, friends. He says plainly that he has no praise to offer.

The answer is False. The text says, "…I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it." (1 Corinthians 11:18) Paul believes at least part of the report, friends. He didn't throw it out.

The answer is which of them are approved. Paul says, “…there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.” (1 Corinthians 11:19) Think of approved like a cookie that passes inspection and gets sealed in the box. The differences bring that out into the open. Paul has just said he hears of divisions among them when they come together as a church (verse 18).

The answer is True. Paul says, “…as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal.” (1 Corinthians 11:21) Then he adds, “While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.” Eating together is supposed to mean, well, together, friends.

The answer is homes. Paul asks, "Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink?" (1 Corinthians 11:22) It's a pointed question, friends. If you're just filling your own plate, your kitchen table can do that.

The answer is those who have nothing. Paul asks if they "…humiliate those who have nothing?" (1 Corinthians 11:22) Those are the ones he's asking about, friends. It's the person at the table with empty hands.
The answer is False. Paul says he received it "…from the Lord…" (1 Corinthians 11:23) Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles (Matthew 10:2), isn't named as the source. Paul points straight to the Lord.
The answer is to remember Him. Jesus says, "do this in remembrance of Me." (1 Corinthians 11:24) That's His reason, friends, right in His own words. Simple and clear.

The answer is the new covenant in His blood. Jesus says, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood…” (1 Corinthians 11:25) A covenant is a binding agreement, and Jesus says this new one is in His blood. Paul ties the cup to Jesus' death: as often as they eat the bread and drink the cup, they proclaim the Lord's death until He comes (verse 26). And Jesus says to do it in remembrance of Him.

The answer is death. Paul says, "…you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes." (1 Corinthians 11:26) Every time they eat the bread and drink the cup, friends, they're proclaiming it. And it goes on until He comes.

The answer is the body and blood of the Lord. Paul says that person "…will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord." (1 Corinthians 11:27) That's serious language, friends. It's about the Lord's own body and blood.

The answer is examine. Paul says, “Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.” (1 Corinthians 11:28) It's a look in the mirror before the table, friends. The word is examine, and it comes before the eating and drinking. Paul asks it of each one.

The answer is judgment. Paul says that person "…eats and drinks judgment on himself." (1 Corinthians 11:29) That's the weight of the thing, friends. Without recognizing the body, that's what's being eaten and drunk.
The answer is True. Paul says, "Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment." (1 Corinthians 11:31) Notice the "we," friends. He includes himself.

The answer is so we won't be condemned with the world. Paul says, "…we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world." (1 Corinthians 11:32) That's the purpose he gives, friends. It's discipline, and discipline has a goal.

The answer is wait for one another. Paul says, “…when you come together to eat, wait for one another.” (1 Corinthians 11:33) Plain and simple, friends. Earlier he said that as they eat, each one goes ahead without sharing (1 Corinthians 11:21). Now his instruction is to wait for one another.

The answer is so coming together won't result in judgment. Paul says, “If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment.” (1 Corinthians 11:34) That's his reason, friends, in his words. The hungry one eats at home, so the coming together doesn't result in judgment.
